transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Ross (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Head of Platform, Luma), Priya Rao (CTO, Luma), Sam Torres (SRE, Luma)

Summary: quick renewal + expansion check-in. Luma on Redwood Hosted today, evaluating Dedicated capacity and adding APAC region; discussing contract extension timing, pricing, and security compliance. Agreed to run a dedicated benchmark in APAC and share pricing/TCO.

Topics: renewal timing, capacity upgrade (dedicated GPUs), additional regions (APAC, EU), contract extension length and discounts, security docs (SOC2/KMS/VPC), bench runs and success criteria.

00:00 Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for making time, we got Priya and Sam on the line as well.
00:12 Maya Patel: thanks Jordan, appreciate it; quick agenda - renewal timeline, proposed capacity increase, APAC region onboarding and pricing, and next steps. Evan will run the belt and tech details.
00:28 Evan Ross: hi all, quick note - apologies if audio pops, i'm on a train, but should be fine. so Luma today is on the hosted plan, right? can you confirm current qps and token volumes?
00:45 Jordan Kim: yeah right now our workload is about 1.2M tokens/day, peaks around 250 qps during billing windows; most traffic is NA but we've seen growth in APAC - about 18% of traffic and growing.
01:03 Priya Rao: main ask from execs is predictable latency under 400ms p95 for user-facing flows, and cost needs to stay within our forecast; also we need to extend contract to align with fiscal year.
01:18 Evan Ross: got it; on hosted we've seen you hit soft limits in late March, Maya mentioned. dedicated would give predictable throughput and lower p95 due to reserved GPUs and colocated APAC nodes.
01:33 Sam Torres: anomaly - late March we hit a KV cache invalidation that added latency - want to understand how Redwood handles cache warming across regions.
01:49 Evan Ross: yes, so runtime has prefix/KV cache and we can pre-warm during onboarding; when we replicate to APAC we'll do a staged sync so cold-starts are limited. sometimes notes in the logs show 'redwind' instead of 'redwood' in auto transcripts, ha.
02:06 Maya Patel: ha, classic. ok on pricing - i'll share a TCO with dedicated sku options (2x, 4x current throughput) and multi-region addon.
02:20 Jordan Kim: timeline - we're aiming to commit by end of April so alignment with your renewal counts. would that work?
02:31 Maya Patel: yes that gives us time - we'll send pricing by Monday and propose contract amendment for 12-24 months with tiered discounting for multi-region.
02:45 Evan Ross: technical: for APAC we recommend a dedicated pool in GCP ap-northeast with 4 GPUs to start, can autoscale within policy; for EU we can plan later. how sensitive is Luma to cold-start token cost vs stable throughput?
03:03 Priya Rao: cost is important; we want to keep per-token unit cost under target but accept slightly higher cost if latency improves. also need SOC2 & KMS details for procurement.
03:20 Maya Patel: we'll attach SOC2 report and KMS/HSM integration docs; Redwood Private options exist but seems like dedicated hosted with VPC peering should solve your data in transit/at rest requirements.
03:36 Jordan Kim: what about data residency - can we pin APAC region so logs/audit stay in APAC?
03:46 Evan Ross: yes logs and KV cache replicas can be configured per-region; audit logs go to your S3 in region if you set up the integration, we'll share the onboarding doc.
03:58 Sam Torres: curious on SLOs - do dedicated customers get latency SLA?
04:08 Maya Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA appendix in the quote.
04:18 Jordan Kim: great. Evan, can you run through the benchmark plan? we want a fairness run comparing hosted vs dedicated in APAC.
04:28 Evan Ross: sure - propose 3 phases: 1) baseline hosted run with sample traffic (48h), 2) dedicated cluster run with same traffic profile, 3) soak test at 2x peak to validate autoscale. measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, and cold-start incidence. I'll provide the script and infra hooks.
04:48 Priya Rao: timeline for that?
04:52 Evan Ross: earliest is week of 2026-04-27; need Luma to share traffic profiles and give infra access for VPN/VPC peering; figure 72 hours of runs.
05:05 Jordan Kim: we'll aim to have profiles to you by Apr 21.
05:10 Maya Patel: noted. on pricing - a couple things to consider: reserved vs on-demand dedicated commit, and multi-region discounting. we'll model both in the TCO.
05:23 Jordan Kim: on contract length - our FP&A prefers 24 months for budget predictability. would Redwood offer additional discount for 24-month commit?
05:34 Maya Patel: yes, typical is incremental discount for longer commit and for capacity thresholds; i'll include scenarios: 12 months, 24 months, and 24 months + APAC add-on.
05:47 Priya Rao: procurement will need SOC2, penetration test summary, SSO/SAML setup and RBAC in console. also need a sample DPA.
06:02 Maya Patel: we'll attach SOC2 and DPA; SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported - Evan can share the admin flow.
06:12 Evan Ross: admin setup includes SAML + SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC roles for route-level permissions; we also log token-level usage in console for cost tracking.
06:24 Sam Torres: any concerns about KV cache replication causing data leakage across tenants?
06:32 Evan Ross: KV cache is per-customer and encrypted; cross-tenant leakage is prevented by tenant isolation at the runtime layer; we'll include the architecture diagram.
06:44 Jordan Kim: competitors - we're also talking to Anthropic and evaluating some internal self-host experiments. openai's platform is baseline for pricing.
06:57 Maya Patel: understood, we'll make sure the TCO shows clear latency/cost tradeoffs.
07:05 Priya Rao: what about burst capacity during product launches? sometimes we need +3x capacity for a day or two.
07:14 Evan Ross: Dedicated can be configured with burst pools and autoscale policies; there's also an optional burst credit that we can include for rare spikes.
07:25 Jordan Kim: what is the expected lead time to add APAC nodes once we sign?
07:31 Maya Patel: with approvals and peering in place, about 7-10 business days to stand up a dedicated APAC pool and do onboarding. the benchmark run can start as soon as infra access is provided.
07:46 Sam Torres: ok. another question - do we get separate billing per-region?
07:52 Maya Patel: we can provide per-region usage breakdowns and separate billing lines if you prefer; helps internal chargeback.
08:02 Jordan Kim: useful. are there any limits to model variants we can run? we sometimes want different quantization profiles.
08:10 Evan Ross: runtime supports multiple model variants and quant profiles; we can pin models per-route and roll out canary style. quantization recommendations will be in the optimize report.
08:24 Priya Rao: for the renewal, is there any penalty or proration if we expand mid-contract?
08:30 Maya Patel: expansions are typically additive; we can do amendment to add capacity and prorate to next renewal date or extend term - we'll propose options.
08:42 Jordan Kim: great. let's talk success criteria for the pilot - what would Redwood need?
08:48 Evan Ross: success = p95 < 400ms for user flows in APAC on dedicated, sustained throughput >= 2x current peak, and token unit cost within agreed TCO band. also no security blockers from procurement.
09:05 Maya Patel: i'll include those as acceptance criteria in the pilot doc.
09:12 Jordan Kim: rough numbers - what's the expected delta in per-token cost moving to dedicated?
09:18 Maya Patel: depends on utilization and commit level; ballpark 15-30% savings at moderate commit; i'll show both conservative and optimistic cases.
09:28 Priya Rao: make sure the TCO includes networking egress in APAC; that can be material.
09:36 Evan Ross: good call - we'll include egress and peering costs.
09:42 Jordan Kim: procurement will also ask about incident response and playbooks.
09:47 Maya Patel: we'll share our incident response summary and escalation contacts; dedicated customers can opt for premium SLA + 24/7 on-call.
09:58 Sam Torres: ok, operational question - what observability do we get? traces, token-level cost, route-level latency?
10:06 Evan Ross: yes console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, tracing hooks and logs export; we'll provide demo link if useful.
10:18 Jordan Kim: fine, might want a short demo for SREs.
10:22 Maya Patel: happy to schedule a 30-min SE demo after pricing and before the benchmark.
10:30 Priya Rao: last for now - anything in the contract about backup/retention?
10:35 Maya Patel: retention policies and logs retention are configurable; the DPA will spell retention windows and deletion flows.
10:43 Jordan Kim: ok thanks, i think next steps are clear.
10:48 Maya Patel: recap - Maya sends pricing/TCO and SLA appendix by 2026-04-20, Evan sends benchmark plan and scripts by 2026-04-24, Luma (Jordan) shares traffic profile by 2026-04-21. we'll aim to run benchmarks week of 2026-04-27.
10:58 Priya Rao: sounds good.
11:02 Jordan Kim: any blockers?
11:04 Sam Torres: none from infra beyond peering setup.
11:07 Maya Patel: great, i'll open a support ticket to start peering checklist and include Evan.
11:13 Evan Ross: i'll draft the plan and include metric collection points.
11:17 Jordan Kim: thanks everyone.
11:20 Maya Patel: thanks all, talk soon.

Action recap at end of call: send pricing, SOC2, DPA, benchmark plan, share traffic profiles, schedule demo for SREs.

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcript notes - occasional mis-attributions and typos (e.g., 'redwind' for Redwood), filler words, and some run-on lines.

End of transcript.
